notes: Access: direct fetch worked throughout (no WAF/block); robots.txt (https://www.nitori-net.jp/robots.txt) has only generic query-string disallows, no Claude-specific rule. Platform is SAP Commerce Cloud (Spartacus/hybris) — confirmed via an embedded <script id="nitoristore-state" type="application/json"> SSR state blob present on every /ec/cat/<path>/1/ page, which contains the exact product-search-results object the Angular storefront hydrates from: pagination.totalResults/totalPages/pageSize plus the full product list and a categories breadcrumb (facetValueName) giving the true Japanese category name independent of the URL's English slug. Category tree discovered via sitemap_item_1.xml (https://www.nitori-net.jp/ecstatic/sitemap/sitemap.xml -> sitemap_item_1.xml), which lists ~816 distinct /ec/cat/ leaf URLs across ~35 top-level departments; each candidate decor-relevant leaf was fetched directly and its qty taken from pagination.totalResults (this is a first-party SSR search-API total, not a Shopify/Magento/Searchspring-style count, but Rule 1 exhaustion-checked anyway: WallInteriorPoster page 2 returned 42 distinct additional titles matching 102-60=42, and ClockTable page 2 returned distinct additional titles consistent with its total minus page 1 — no signs of inflation. ClockTable showed 95 on first fetch vs 97 on a later page-2 fetch, a 2-unit drift consistent with normal live-inventory turnover, not a counting-method artifact; qty recorded uses the first canonical fetch, 95). Rule 0 gains: traversed the entire Lighting_Fixture branch (9 leaf nodes) with no depth limit, including motion/sensor lights (OtherLightingSensor) and clip-on lamps, which are easy to miss; captured all 3 Mirror sub-types (stand/table/wall) and all 5 Clock sub-types (alarm/pendulum/radio-controlled/table/wall) despite Clock living under the generic 'LifeSuppliesDailyNecessities' (daily necessities) department, not an obviously-decor-named branch. Clock sub-categories (Table/Wall/Radio-Controlled) likely share some overlapping dual-use SKUs (many product titles are literally '掛け置き兼用時計' = wall-or-table dual-use clock) — emitted as separate site-native leaf categories per Rule 0.6 rather than merged/deduped, since the site itself lists them as first-class distinct category codes. Duplicate-company: none — this is the project's first Nitori entry, not flagged in the brief's duplicate list. Mixed roll-up handling (brief Rule: 'drop, don't pad — inspect actual titles'): (1) InteriorArticleDoll ('オブジェ・置物' = Objects/Ornaments, 56 items) DROPPED ENTIRELY after full title inspection — only 23/56 are genuine decor objects (storm glasses, Galileo thermometers, ornament coin-bank figurines, brass card stands, marble/wood coasters); the majority 33/56 are keychain charms and acrylic character-mascot goods (チャーム, アクリルチャーム, アクリルキーホルダー — Snoopy/mascot keyholders), i.e. novelty gift accessories, not home decor, so the category was dropped rather than partially padded. (2) CandleAromaoilCandle ('キャンドル・キャンドルホルダー' = Candles & Candle Holders, 17 items, complete single-page listing) manually curated to qty 8: kept unscented/novelty candles and candle holders (wood crackle-sound candle, 2x glass candles, explicitly-labelled '無香料'/unscented 48-pack, 2x candle holders, 1 more candle), excluded 9 items that were アロマキャンドル (scented aroma candles x2), a candle-warmer lamp/light x2 (fragrance-wax-melt appliances), パロサントスティック (palo santo incense stick), アロマストーン (aroma diffuser stone), and 2 incense-ash holders (香立て) — all home-fragrance/incense, excluded per brief. Exclusions applied after title review: AromaDiffuserAroma/CandleAromaoilAroma (home fragrance diffusers/oils, 143+27 items), Christmas branch and FakegreenArtificial (artificial flowers/holiday, excluded categories), Foliage_Plant (real potted houseplants — gardening, not a decor accessory type on the brief's include list), WallInteriorCorkboard (turned out to be whiteboards, office supply not decor), WallInteriorShelf (wall shelving = storage furniture), WallInteriorwallstickers (turned out to be peelable WALLPAPER/wall panels, explicitly excluded), WallInterior/Switchcover (1 item, an outlet safety guard), WallInteriorOther ('壁掛けフック・金具' = wall hooks & metal fittings — inspected titles are all functional mounting hardware: adjuster hooks, magnet hooks, picture-rail wire, ceiling pin hooks, bath hooks; hardware, not decorative wall art), CurtainArticleHook (curtain-rail runners/adjuster clips — small hardware fasteners, distinct from the included Fusakake/Tassel tiebacks), Lighting_Fixture/LEDbulb and lighting/CeilingFan (bulbs/fans explicitly excluded even though co-located with in-scope lighting), Tableware/TablewareCutlery (fork/knife/spoon/chopsticks — cutlery excluded), Tableware/GlassMugPotPot (inspected titles are all coffee-drip equipment — coffee dripper sets, brewing gear — kitchen tool, not tableware, despite the 'Pot' slug suggesting teapots), Tableware/WaterBarrel ('ピッチャー・冷水筒' = pitchers & fridge cold-water jugs — functional kitchen storage container, not a decorative/display tableware piece), Tableware/TablewareTableware ('お酒グッズ・ワイングッズ' = wine/bar goods — wine coolers, ice pails, bottle stoppers — bar tools, excluded), Tableware/KitchenFabricTablecloth and KitchenTray's fabric coasters/placemats (textiles), GardeningLeisureOutdoor/PlanterVacePlanter (199 items; title-inspected and found to be almost entirely functional plastic nursery pots ('プラ鉢') and plant display racks/stands (furniture), not decorative planters — kept the sibling PlanterVaceCover, decorative pot covers, and PlanterVaceVace, actual flower vases, both of which title-inspection confirmed as genuine decor), BathToiletLaundry branch in full (bath bottles/storage/mats/shower heads/soap dishes — functional bath fixtures/storage/plumbing, no item found that was a purely decorative bathroom accessory distinct from a fixture), LifeSuppliesDailyNecessities/Clock/ClockSmartWatch (wearable electronics, not home decor despite living in the Clock facet), all of CurtainRailBlind's fabric curtains/lace/blinds/roll-screens/noren (textiles/window-treatment hardware, not decorative metal), and the entire furniture-coded top-level departments (Bed, Chair, Sofa, Storage-Furniture, StorageRackDresser, TvStandLivingStorage, CupboardApplianceBoard, Kotatu, TableChair, Desk-Officechair, Mattress, CarpetRugMat/rugs=textile), Appliance/Baby/Pet/RelaxHealth/Roomwear/SeniorGoods/OfficeBookshelfStationery/OutdoorTravel/Houjin(B2B) departments (no decor content). Kept 'Tableware/dinnerware' filed under 'Kitchen & Dining' per brief's own filing instruction, combined with all Glassware sub-types (beer/wine/tumbler/mug/cup-saucer/sake-tokkuri/Japanese-teacup) since the brief lists glassware as always in-scope. Curtain rails/poles and tiebacks/tassels kept as 'Curtain Hardware' per brief's explicit 'decorative metal ... curtain rods/tiebacks' inclusion, even though most individual curtain-rail SKUs are technical/motorised rail hardware rather than ornamental rods — included on the strength of the brief's explicit named inclusion. All category/sub_category names are English translations of the Japanese facetValueName values read from each page's own breadcrumb (not guessed from the URL's transliterated slug, which was sometimes misleading, e.g. 'InteriorArticleDoll' slug vs actual 'オブジェ・置物'/Objects-Ornaments name).
